history.summary: IMPORTANT: this is NOT the same shrine as seq 405 (Rankini Mandir, Rohinibera/Jadugora, ~35 km away) - it is the separate, older in-city Rankini temple in Kadma, Jamshedpur, which reviews describe as one of the oldest temples in Jamshedpur. Much published web history conflates this Kadma shrine with the Jadugora/Kapadgadi Rankini shrine (1947-50 foundation by Dinbandhu Singh, narabali until ~1865, Bhumij tribal origins, 'living stone' idol): IDENTITY/HISTORY CONFLATION - treat Jadugora-specific claims as (verify) for the Kadma temple. Local sources describe the Kadma temple as a simple, serene complex dedicated to Goddess Rankini (a regional form of Kali/Parvati) with adjoining shrines for Ram-Sita, Hanuman, Radha-Krishna, Shiva, Maa Kali, Navagraha and Shitla Devi. Durga Puja is its biggest festival. A third, smaller 'Sri Sri Rankini Mandir' also exists near Jail Chowk, Sakchi - note the naming collision. CSV town 'Jamshedpur' is coarse - corrected to Kadma, Jamshedpur.

name: Rankini Temple
town_description: Jamshedpur, known as the Steel City of India, is the largest city in Jharkhand. Founded by Jamsetji Tata as a planned industrial town around Tata Steel (TISCO), the settlement was called Sakchi until it was renamed Jamshedpur in 1919. The city sits at the confluence of the Kharkai and Subarnarekha rivers in East Singhbhum district, and its neighbourhoods (Telco, Golmuri, Sakchi, Kadma, Parsudih, Sidhgora) grew around Tata Steel and its subsidiary companies.

travel.road: Kadma is a central Jamshedpur locality, reachable by city bus, auto and taxi

visitor_information.best_time: October to February (winter); Durga Puja is the major festival period
